children: Joby Aviation, Inc. (
JOBY

is grabbing everyone’s attention with its latest announcement related to automation aviation expansion. To this end, Joby Aviation recently announced the successful execution of its first-ever autonomous flight across the United States. The aircraft flew 3,199 miles with zero control inputs from its onboard safety pilot and concluded the eastbound leg of its month-long tour in North Carolina’s Outer Banks.

The aircraft equipped with its autonomy technology is a converted Cessna Caravan. The aircraft has carried out autonomous taxiing, takeoffs, route navigation and landings under remote supervision from JOBY’s Autonomy Headquarters in California and Shaw Air Force Base in South Carolina, up to 2,323 miles away. The journey reflected the operational capabilities of JOBY’s autonomy technology across a variety of environments while boosting applications in commercial freight, medical transport, disaster response and defense logistics.

During the cross-country journey, the aircraft proved its potential to easily integrate into high-density environments like Phoenix Deer Valley (a busy general aviation airport) while rerouting around severe weather and thunderstorms in real time with no prior airport familiarity.

As part of Joby Aviation’s 2026 Electric Skies tour, the eastbound leg featured flight demonstrations, logistics showcases and key operational milestones across the following stops, namely, Concord, CA (KCCR), Phoenix, AZ (KDVT), Fort Worth, TX (KAFW), Shaw Air Force Base, SC (KSSC) and Outer Banks, NC (KMQI). The aircraft plans to start its return westbound journey, which includes stops in Raleigh (KRDU), Fredericksburg/Washington, D.C. (KRMN), Louisville (KSDF), Wichita (KICT), Oklahoma City (KOKC), Salt Lake City (KSLC), and Portland (KPDX).

Built on the mature autonomy stack purchased from Xwing in 2024, Joby Aviation’s autonomous technology is grounded in more than 400 flights and 800 automated flight hours in controlled and uncontrolled airspace. JOBY plans to provide a scalable path to autonomous air logistics through the merger of an autonomous system onto an already-certified airframe.

JoeBen Bevirt, founder and chief executive officer of Joby Aviation, stated, “This journey across America offers a glimpse into a new era of aviation. Autonomy has an important role to play in the future of flight, allowing us to connect remote communities, deliver critical supplies, respond faster to disasters, support military operations, and keep pilots out of harm’s way.”
